pr_title: Propagate last node to reinitialized routing tables
pr_body:
When closing or opening an index, or restoring a snapshot over a closed index, we reinitialize its routing table from scratch and expect the gateway allocators to select the appropriate node for each shard copy. With this commit we also keep track of the last-allocated node ID for each copy which makes it more likely that the desired balance of these shards remains unchanged too.

Closes #91472

comments: I'm struggling to reproduce this, but I suspect there might be a state where there are no relocating shards but a desired balance computation is still in flight, and then the computation completes and triggers some relocations, and the state on which the assertion trips includes some relocating shards on its way to a properly balanced state.

> I suspect there might be a state where there are no relocating shards but a desired balance computation is still in flight

I reproduced this failure eventually (after several hours of successful runs) and found that this is indeed the case. Moreover the reason we end up in an unbalanced state seems to be related to allocating the shards after closing the index: the actual allocation is handled by the gateway allocators but the desired balance allocator sometimes makes subtly different decisions and the cluster performs a rebalancing move after settling. I believe the problem might be that we do not set `UnassignedInfo#lastAllocatedNodeId` when closing (or opening) an index, but I'm still working to confirm this.

> I believe the problem might be that we do not set `UnassignedInfo#lastAllocatedNodeId` when closing (or opening) an index, but I'm still working to confirm this.

Confirmed this, and opened #91549 to fix it.

review_comments: Can this not go one line up, i.e., we can check this for every shard id?
Not if the shard count can change in a restore (which AFAIK it can)

I think only the number of replicas, not the number of shards can be changed? Probably what you meant with shards/replicas, but removing "shards/" would be better I think.
```suggestion
                    // restoring an index may change the number of replicas so no guarantee that lastAllocatedNodeId is populated
```
On the contrary, I didn't think there's anything to require that the snapshot has the same number of shards as index on top of which it's being restored.

This also includes the target of relocations. I wonder if we should only look at active shards, since anything less will anyway not be considered good enough by the gateway allocator?

The problem I see with this is that if a relocation is ongoing, we risk a copy having a last allocated node id that is much worse than it could be (i.e., a node that only has just started the recovery)?
